items.title: Veilwing · wingbeat cycle
items.creator_request: different stages of flight to get that anatomy down
items.description: Previously approved flight study, retained as history. Its one-dorsal count is superseded by the creator’s latest choice of two back sails plus two front shoulder wings.
items.prompt:
1536x1024 landscape. A clean Breachline FLIGHT-ANATOMY contact sheet on plain warm ivory paper. Exactly FOUR separate full-body drawings of the SAME individual Veilwing in a spacious 2-column by 2-row layout. Each whole animal, feelers, sail tips and all three streamers stays inside its quadrant with margins, no overlap between quadrants. No text, labels, arrows, numbers, borders or scenery. Measured pencil/brush contour, pale amber translucent membrane washes, sparse mauve veins and quiet anatomical shading, matching the attached structural reference. Use the source's LARGE side view as identity; do not copy its extra small inset into any panel.

INVARIANTS IN ALL FOUR PANELS: exactly ONE unpaired dorsal sail attached on the spinal midline at MID-BACK, distinctly behind the shoulder station; exactly TWO side wings attached at the same fore-aft station on opposing SHOULDER FLANKS. Exactly three main sail surfaces. The side-wing ROOTS stay at the shoulders during every stroke: only rotation and elastic bending change. The dorsal ROOT stays at mid-back during every pose, separated from the shoulder roots by exposed back. Its sail can flex slightly with airflow but does not migrate forward, duplicate, become a second pair or substitute for an occluded side wing. Retain the same long pointed head, paired fine head feelers, slender torso length, relative sail sizes, lobed membrane outlines and exactly three long leaf-tipped tail ribbons. No legs, claws, hands, bird elbows or added skeletal appendages. Do not thicken the body into a bird. No harness or passengers; expose the anatomy. Foreshorten and occlude surfaces honestly. Dorsal and lateral roots must remain distinguishable even when their tips overlap. These are exploratory motion poses, not new species or redesigns.

This sheet tests the WINGBEAT. Use the SAME shallow side/front three-quarter camera in every cell, the same left-facing head, same level horizontal torso attitude and same scale. The neck/torso/root stations should line up conceptually across the four images. The front pair of side wings move together through the cycle while the single aft dorsal sail stays upright relative to the spine. Keep its height and profile consistent so it serves as a stable reference.

TOP LEFT: LEVEL GLIDE. Both side wings spread laterally in a shallow nearly horizontal flight plane. Near wing projects toward viewer; far wing correctly foreshortened behind the body. One tall dorsal sail rises from mid-back, aft of the wing roots.
TOP RIGHT: RAISED RECOVERY. Both SHOULDER wings raised about 50 degrees above their level-glide position in a matched upstroke. Roots remain at the shoulders. The side wings are forward of the dorsal, which remains on MID-BACK. Show all three attachment locations through clear offset silhouettes and honest overlap. The outer membranes bow softly and trail; no new dorsal surfaces.
BOTTOM LEFT: MID-DOWNSTROKE. Shoulder wings sweep downward through the horizontal, broad membranes slightly cupped and tension carried along their leading edges. Show a different shape from the flat glide, with a small elastic lag of the trailing edges. Torso and aft dorsal remain steady; no shifted joints.
BOTTOM RIGHT: LOW STROKE. Both shoulder wings extend downward about 45 degrees below horizontal with tips trailing gently back. Root heights remain matched. Show near wing down toward viewer and far wing down away, both clearly emerging from the SAME shoulder station, not attached to the tail. Mid-back dorsal remains tall above the torso.

Keep the differences between the four stages large enough to read immediately. Do not simply repeat the glide four times. Do not flatten the dorsal during the downstroke or move it onto a lateral wing. Maintain the graceful original animal throughout.

Its rich varied mottling and draping biological forms are essential. Do not turn it into a smooth long-necked snake or bird. IMAGE 2 is ONLY the approved structural guide for sail attachment and perspective, not a reason to replace image 1's body, skin, colour or silhouette.

CORRECT ANATOMY: exactly TWO huge opposing SHOULDER wings at the same fore-aft station and exactly ONE dorsal sail rooted farther back at MID-BACK. The two main lateral wings are expansively large, as newly requested. Keep one mid-back dorsal at its established scale; never add a second dorsal or fourth membrane. Resolve the near-wing root which was ambiguous in image 1. Let both side wings visibly connect continuously to their own flanks and foreshorten honestly. The dorsal can overlap them but must emerge from a separate spinal root well behind the shoulders. Keep image 1's beautiful leaflike body surfaces, paired delicate head feelers and exactly three long leaf-tipped rear ribbons.

POSE AND SETTING: retain a largely sideways three-quarter view similar in appeal to image 1, with a GENTLE ASCENDING BANK TO THE ANIMAL'S OWN RIGHT so a little of its underside is visible. The animal's right wing is somewhat lower, left wing higher; rotate torso and dorsal coherently. Head toward upper left, tail flowing lower right. Do not stretch its neck to obtain the upward pose. Entire silhouette fits with breathing room. Fly VERY HIGH above a settled river landscape; tiny roofs, fields, woods and a stone crossing are far below through atmospheric haze. Warm, natural, luminous daylight through the sails, quieter soft land forms. The beast is graceful and immense, not menacing.

HARNESS: return to image 1's plain functional matte brown LEATHER BACK HARNESS with slim longitudinal leather connections and simple fitted body bands. This is not the recent woven collar/pendant; no scarf, patterned neckwear, satchel, badge or decorative panel. Refine the R2 fit around the CORRECT intact anatomy: a band on the bare upper chest just ahead of the shoulder roots, a second band around the robust torso behind the shoulder station but BEFORE the mid-back dorsal starts. A short upper connecting strap follows the bare spinal surface between these bands, passing above and between the two shoulder roots without touching their membranes. The fitting stays entirely forward of the dorsal base; no strap crosses the dorsal or binds a side wing. Trace the real body's contours. Do not add a new strap over a sail to complete the old image's belt layout.

EXTREME SCALE: the animal is huge, comparable in presence to a flying whale; its body is on the scale of a long building. This is an image scale cue, not new species dimensions. The R2 harness looked attractive but its buckles were much too large. Make the straps visually slender relative to the body and the fastenings TINY, with minute repeated stitching/joins indicating human craftsmanship. Avoid giant easy-to-read single buckles: hardware should look small enough for a person to handle against a vast expanse of animal. The harness's visual weight must stay modest. No riders, seats, platforms, gondolas, reins, bits, cargo or people aboard. This individual willingly works with nature-minded Gnosis practitioners through a respectful magical connection; equipment shows familiar care, no visible magical spectacle required.

Traditional oil/acrylic fantasy painting with selective visible brushwork, matte hide and leather, softly translucent mottled membranes, one coherent light source, much less detail in the distant ground. Edit this ORIGINAL R2 painting into a corrected creature reference. This exact image is the authority for the long slender character, colours, head, harness, tail texture and quiet painted atmosphere. Do not substitute the short thick drake-like body of the later studies. Preserve the original muted warm ivory, dusty lavender and ochre, soft coherent light and oil/acrylic paint handling. Ancient strength and mystery: a slender, long, immense creature with enormous wings and gently flowing tails.

CORRECT THE CONTINUOUS BODY FIRST. In the original, the slender torso carrying the harness seems to continue right beneath the middle sail, while a different branch below it carries the tails too early. These must be ONE body, not a fork. Follow the beautiful long slender contour of the harness-bearing torso. Extend that single continuous body beneath the big middle/front dorsal sail toward its lower trailing pointed tip, ending just BEFORE that tip, not past it. In the original coordinates, the real rump should end near x900,y490, approaching but staying short of the middle sail's lower point near x970,y530. This is a broad spatial guide, not a contour to trace. Keep the body elegant and slim with an uninterrupted subtle shaded underside; do not make a fat belly or a long thin neck. No second torso hanging below it. The sail stays a distinct mobile membrane above that body with its own free edge and root.

TAILS: remove the premature tail-bearing branch beneath midbody. All FOUR tails now grow naturally from the single true posterior end of the lengthened torso. Preserve what is beautiful in R2: each tail begins with a substantial softly feathered taper, becomes a very long thin supple stem, and opens into a modest leaflike terminal fan. Four complete tails, four fans, no additional bare filaments. They drift in graceful different curves as if in a gentle breeze, not straight wires or identical ribbons. Make them a little longer than R2's tails; their total curving length is at least comparable to the NEW long snout-to-rump body. Never shorten them to fit the page. Pull back the framing uniformly enough to fit every tip with breathing room while preserving the longer body and enormous wing scale.

ADD THE MISSING NEAR LEFT SHOULDER WING. We are viewing the left side. The visible shoulder between the FIRST TWO leather buckles nearest the head is currently bare. A huge LEFT front wing must grow from that gap, from the lateral shoulder beneath the top leather connector. Keep the original existing downstroking RIGHT/front wing on the far side; the creator likes it. The new left wing attaches directly opposite that existing right wing at the SAME shoulder cross-section, not from the middle or rear of the body. It is the same actual anatomical wing type: very large broad leaf-feather membrane, curved leading edge, scalloped trailing edge and long slender hooked terminal point. Let the near left wing descend into the lower foreground, partly overlapping the existing far/right wing naturally, while keeping BOTH hooked tips visibly separated. Preserve the original right wing's shape; do not replace it with a short triangle. Keep the harness clear of the moving root; no strap through the membrane.

Preserve BOTH original dorsal sails, their broad swept shapes and their separate mobile back attachments. This completes exactly FOUR flight surfaces: left front, right front, front dorsal sail, rear dorsal sail. No fifth membrane, neck flap or belly fin. Keep the original face, feelers, plain leather equipment and natural soft colour. Retain the simple original distant ground/sky only as a quiet backdrop, with no huge shadow or new buildings. No annotations, text or labels. This is the single long-bodied anatomical reference from R2, not a compact new species.
